import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Rational distance problem

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_square#Rational_distance_problem)
- [mathoverflow/418260](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/418260/)
asked by user [Yuan Yang](https://mathoverflow.net/users/177957/yuan-yang)
- D19 in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*
-/

namespace RationalDistanceProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

def UnitSquareCorners : Fin 4 → ℝ² :=
  ![!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]]

/--
Does there exist a point in the plane at rational distance from all four vertices of the unit square?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem rational_distance_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ² , ∀ i, ¬ Irrational (dist P (UnitSquareCorners i)) := by
  sorry

end RationalDistanceProblem

reformulations.difference: Rationality of each distance is expressed as `¬ Irrational (dist P (UnitSquareCorners i))`, rather than by explicitly supplying a rational number for that distance.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib defines `Irrational x` as `x ∉ Set.range (Rat.cast : ℚ → ℝ)`. Classically, its negation is exactly `∃ q : ℚ, (q : ℝ) = x`. Choosing these witnesses for the four indices proves that the theorem's right-hand side is equivalent to `∃ (P : ℝ²) (r : Fin 4 → ℚ), ∀ i, (r i : ℝ) = dist P (UnitSquareCorners i)`. This equivalence was proved in the scratch file without using the problem theorem or any sorry.

sources_consulted: Richard K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0 — publisher metadata and accessible chapter previews/bibliographies; full §D19 unavailable
https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0_5 — Diophantine Equations, particularly the reference to Berry (1990)

T. G. Berry, “Points at rational distance from the corners of a unit square,” Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa 17 (1990), 505–529, introduction and §4: https://www.numdam.org/item/ASNSP_1990_4_17_4_505_0.pdf (text extracted through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.numdam.org/item/ASNSP_1990_4_17_4_505_0.pdf)
review.notes: Both declarations were checked. The corners are the correct four distinct vertices, and ℝ² carries the Euclidean metric, not the function-space sup metric. Wikipedia and MathOverflow explicitly allow a point anywhere in the plane, so no interior restriction is missing. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled successfully and verified the distance formula, rational-witness equivalence, and exclusion of every vertex and the center as trivial solutions. The open status matches the consulted sources; MathOverflow's counterexample concerns only an auxiliary elliptic-curve rank proposal. Guy's full §D19 was inaccessible through Springer, but Berry's introduction explicitly links the matching unrestricted-plane problem to §D19. No checkout files were edited.
